title: A worktree's emptied folder stays "busy" after all its TermAl delegation children completed, so git worktree remove cannot finish
outcome:
Reported by Engram::Opus in mailbox-37bcca97 #82 (2026-09-29 05:28Z). `git worktree remove C:\github\Personal\Engram\.worktrees\standing-approval-stand-in` unregistered the worktree and emptied the folder, then failed with "failed to delete …: Permission denied". A later rmdir of the empty folder fails with "Device or resource busy", also on a retry minutes later. Delegation children had run there: Claude and Kimi reviewers session-8465…8478, and acceptance evaluators session-8479 and session-8482, which ran there because it was the named source root of w-879c75f6e604 (now completed). The same removal worked for .worktrees/named-root-state, whose reviewers had finished longer ago.
Diagnosis by Termal::Opus2 at about 05:35Z, read-only:
- Ruled out a lingering agent process: none of the Claude or Kimi child processes of those sessions remain among termal.exe's children.
- Ruled out Engram control processes: session-8482's `engram control` (pid 63956) is still alive, but a delegation child's connection uses project.root_path, the main checkout, as its current directory (engram_host_adapter.rs:5357/5369; engram_control_transport.rs:286), not the worktree.
- Ruled out Git's fsmonitor daemon: no git.exe is running, and core.fsmonitor is unset.
- The workspace watcher watches every local session's workdir, but prunes roots nested under a watched project root (workspace_watch.rs prune_nested_workspace_file_watch_roots), and Engram is a local project.
Remaining suspect: the host (termal.exe) holding a handle, via the watcher or source-root measurement. Unconfirmed. Resource Monitor's Associated Handles search for "standing-approval-stand-in", or Sysinternals handle.exe (not installed), would name the holder. Greg's pending host restart is a natural test: if rmdir succeeds after it, the host held the folder. termal_name_source_root also refuses to clear the name once the claim is gone ("this session holds no live claim"), so a completed item's named root cannot be un-named by its former holder.
acceptance: After a work item's delegation children complete (and its claim ends), TermAl holds no handle or working directory on that worktree, so git worktree remove succeeds; the holder found in this report is identified and released, with a test or a documented manual check
